text: Composting is an essential component of gardening, as it enhances soil fertility, improves soil structure, and fosters robust plant growth. By incorporating rich, well-rotted compost into garden beds, you can cultivate nutrient-dense soil. This method of enrichment supports a healthy and resilient plant population, as well as reduces the need for chemical fertilizers and pesticides. In addition to promoting soil fertility, composting also mitigates the environmental impact of gardening. Mulching can be achieved by adding 2-3 inches of mulch, such as straw, wood chips, or leaves, around plants to retain soil moisture, suppress weeds, and regulate soil temperature. For an easy mulch application, a simple pile of leaves or a handful of small twigs can be used. By integrating composting and mulching practices, you can enhance the health of your plants while simultaneously reducing your environmental footprint and cultivating a thriving garden.
